title: Why Do We Drop a Ball on New Year's Eve?
description:
Why do we drop a giant ball at New Year? It started as a signal for ships. At sea, sailors worked out where they were with a clock set to home time, and one minute wrong could mean about fifteen miles off course.

So in 1833, the Royal Observatory in Greenwich put a big ball on a mast. Every day at exactly 1 pm it dropped, and ships on the river set their clocks (it still drops today). In 1907, New York borrowed the idea for New Year's Eve, with a glowing ball that dropped at midnight.
